bull.t: Strong revenue growth and improving profitability
bull.b: Dutch Bros has expanded revenue rapidly while moving from historical losses to consistent profitability. This combination indicates growing brand demand and operating scale, providing a stronger base for reinvestment, shop expansion, and further earnings growth over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Large expansion runway and strong new-shop productivity
bull.b: A substantial development pipeline and demonstrated new-shop productivity support continued unit growth beyond the current store base. The path toward roughly 4,000 shops gives Dutch Bros a durable avenue to increase revenue and spread its brand across additional U.S. markets.

bull.t: High customer engagement and successful beverage innovation
bull.b: Deep rewards adoption, rising membership density, and successful product innovation can strengthen repeat visits and customer retention. These capabilities support transaction growth and help Dutch Bros sustain brand relevance as it expands into new markets and broadens its beverage platform.

bear.b: Debt remains substantial relative to equity, even after improving from earlier leverage levels. This capital structure can constrain flexibility if traffic or margins weaken, while debt obligations may compete with expansion spending and other uses of internally generated cash.

bear.t: Input and occupancy costs are pressuring margins
bear.b: Coffee, food, packaging, and higher build-to-suit occupancy costs are creating structural pressure on store economics as the footprint grows. Although SG&A leverage partly offsets these effects, persistent cost inflation could limit margin expansion and reduce the earnings benefit of strong sales growth.

bear.t: Expansion requires heavy capital spending and modest cash conversion
bear.b: Dutch Bros is generating positive free cash flow, but only a modest portion of earnings converts into cash after investment needs. The large capital program required for new shops increases funding demands and leaves less financial capacity for debt reduction or resilience during slower operating periods.
